note: Theory that is heard, not recited: tap the three roots on the staff and hear the chord built on each, follow the chords in order, then in a new order without looking. The old Key selector is now moves (any key), so the title names the key as a param, the text names every chord by its number and never by its letter, and the last line says what stays the same in another key. Works for any instrument, or none.

exercise.title: The 1, 4 and 5 chords in {{=key}}, by ear
exercise.why: Each chord is built on one note of the scale, so once you hear the root move from 1 to 4 to 5, you can name the chord that is playing.

cells.text:
The staff below, the five lines of music, shows the {{=key}} major scale: tap a note to hear it. Tap the three ringed notes, {{1}}, {{4}} and {{5}}.
Then press Play under each chord box below, from left to right, to hear the chord built on each of those notes: the 1, the 4 and the 5 chord.

Press Play below to start the backing track: the 1, 4 and 5 chords and back to 1, one bar each. Call out 1, 4 or 5 as each chord arrives, with the lit box to help.
Keep going until you hear a change coming before the box lights.

Press Play below to start the backing track: the same three chords in a new order. Look away from the screen, call out the number of each chord, and look back to check.
If you lose your place, wait for the 1 chord: it sounds like home, and you can pick the order up again from there.
In another key the chords are new, but the 1, the 4 and the 5 still sound the same.
